questions.prompt: Two separately created objects have equal fields. Which Vitest matcher checks their structure?

choices.text: toEqual.
toBe, because equal fields imply one reference.
toBeDefined, because both objects exist.
toBeTruthy, because both values are objects.

questions.explanation: toEqual compares structure. toBe checks reference identity for objects; defined and truthy checks do not compare fields.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: Vitest toBe checks Object.is equality, toEqual compares structure, and synchronous toThrow requires a function wrapper.

questions.prompt: A test asserts a rejected promise using rejects.toThrow. What must the test do with that assertion?

choices.text: Call it without await because rejects is synchronous.
Replace the rejection with a truthy check on the promise.
End the test before the asynchronous matcher settles.
Await the assertion promise.

questions.explanation: Promise matchers are asynchronous. Awaiting them ensures the assertion is completed; promise existence does not verify its outcome.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: Vitest resolves and rejects unwrap promise outcomes and their matchers must be awaited.

questions.prompt: A spy replaces a real implementation and later tests unexpectedly observe it. What maintenance step is missing?

choices.text: Increase the test timeout instead of restoring it.
Reuse the altered implementation in every later test.
Restore the spy after the test.
Repeat the spy call to make its behavior permanent.

questions.explanation: A spy can alter shared behavior. Restoration returns the original implementation and prevents leakage; longer timeouts do not address state.

sources.title: Vitest mocking guide
sources.claim: Vitest mocks and spies record calls and require clearing or restoring state between tests.

questions.prompt: A test waits several real seconds for a scheduled callback. Which tool makes the timer behavior deterministic?

choices.text: Run the test only when the wall clock matches production.
Use fake timers and advance controlled time.
Increase every real delay until CI stops failing.
Skip the callback assertion whenever the machine is busy.

questions.explanation: Fake timers let the test control time without real waiting. Increasing delays and skipping assertions do not test the scheduled behavior reliably.

sources.title: Vitest timers guide
sources.claim: Vitest fake timers simulate timer APIs and can be restored to real timers after a test.

questions.prompt: Which pattern correctly tests a synchronous function that throws?

choices.text: expect(() => operation()).toThrow().
expect(operation()).toThrow(), letting the call throw first.
expect(operation).toBeTruthy(), checking the function exists.
expect(operation()).toBeDefined(), bypassing exception capture.

questions.explanation: The wrapper delays execution until the matcher can capture the error. Existence assertions do not test exceptions.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: Synchronous toThrow needs a function to invoke and capture exceptions.

questions.prompt: An async function should return a known object. Which assertion checks the fulfilled value?

choices.text: expect(operation()).toBe(expected), comparing promise identity.
expect(operation()).toBeTruthy(), checking promise existence.
expect(operation).toBeDefined(), without calling the function.
await expect(operation()).resolves.toEqual(expected).

questions.explanation: resolves unwraps the settled value and toEqual compares it. The alternatives do not test the returned data.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: resolves unwraps a fulfilled promise and must be awaited.

questions.prompt: Which assertion choices match their intended behavior? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Treat toBeTruthy as a complete comparison of object fields.
toEqual proves two objects share the same reference when their fields match.
Use toEqual to compare the structure of separate objects.
Use toBe when object reference identity is the requirement.
Pass an already executed throwing call directly to synchronous toThrow.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Truthy checks boolean conversion, not structure. B is incorrect: Structural equality does not establish reference identity; toBe checks Object.is. C is correct: It compares values recursively. D is correct: toBe uses Object.is semantics. E is incorrect: A function wrapper lets the matcher catch the throw.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: Vitest toBe checks Object.is equality, toEqual compares structure, and synchronous toThrow requires a function wrapper.

questions.prompt: Which async assertion statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: toBe on an unresolved promise compares its future result automatically.
resolves fails when the supplied promise rejects.
rejects fails when the supplied promise fulfills.
Await matchers chained after resolves or rejects.
An existing Promise object proves its eventual result is correct.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: A direct comparison does not unwrap the promise. B is correct: It expects a fulfilled outcome. C is correct: It expects a rejected outcome. D is correct: Those matchers return promises. E is incorrect: The object says nothing about its settled value.

sources.title: Vitest expect API
sources.claim: Vitest resolves and rejects unwrap promise outcomes and their matchers must be awaited.

questions.prompt: Which practices keep mock-based tests isolated? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Clear call history when a new test must start with no previous calls.
Restore spied implementations when replacement is no longer needed.
Assume a mock automatically proves the real dependency behaves identically.
Share accumulated call history to make tests independent.
A spy always replaces the implementation rather than merely observing it.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Recorded interactions can otherwise leak between tests. B is correct: Restoration undoes altered behavior. C is incorrect: A mock supplies controlled behavior rather than validating the real dependency. D is incorrect: Shared state creates order dependence. E is incorrect: A spy can observe existing behavior or be configured with a replacement.

sources.title: Vitest mocking guide
sources.claim: Vitest mocks and spies record calls and require clearing or restoring state between tests.

questions.prompt: Which choices support testing timer-based logic? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Restore real timers when the timer test finishes.
Expect real wall-clock waiting to advance every fake timer automatically.
Use timer controls to trigger scheduled callbacks deterministically.
Treat fake timers as a substitute for asserting callback results.
Enable fake timers before scheduling the behavior under test.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Cleanup avoids affecting later tests. B is incorrect: Fake timer progression is controlled rather than ordinary elapsed time. C is correct: The test can move simulated time forward. D is incorrect: Controlling time does not verify the resulting behavior. E is correct: The scheduled timer must use the controlled timer APIs.

sources.title: Vitest timers guide
sources.claim: Vitest fake timers simulate timer APIs and can be restored to real timers after a test.
